title: OpenAI compatibility: invocation envelope bridge and deterministic tool-selection semantics
author: Leah Kim
description: Motivation: downstream integrations relying on OpenAI-style function/tool calls observed ambiguous tool_choice behavior under concurrent streaming and partial responses. This PR introduces a compatibility "invocation envelope bridge" that 1) projects Redwood's internal tool schema into OpenAI functions at runtime with explicit mapping metadata, 2) standardizes a deterministic tool-selection resolution algorithm for tool_choice hints emitted during partial streams, and 3) reforms the streaming message envelope so third-party adapters can unambiguously reconstruct function/tool invocation intent. Key changes: schema projection table for name/type/coerce rules, deterministic selection policy (rank + deterministic tiebreaker based on stable schema id), streaming fragments include an envelope header with stable tool_id and schema_version, and backward-compatible fallbacks to previous heuristics when compatibility mode is disabled. This is implemented with minimal runtime overhead and guarded behind an opt-in feature flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_BRIDGE) while we validate customer traffic. The description below lists what reviewers should pay attention to: migration notes, performance impact, and streaming stability tests. Migration notes: operators can enable the bridge per-route via the new route option openai_compat.bridge=true or at deployment level; when enabled, existing persisted prompts that relied on old ambiguous selection will behave the same unless reprocessed. Performance: microbenchmark shows ~3% p99 token latency increase in worst-case due to extra envelope serialization, but batch throughput is unchanged. Testing: unit tests for schema translation, deterministic tiebreaker, and e2e streaming test harness added. Docs: added a compatibility guide and examples for SDKs. Related: Linear ENG-4123 and PM-987. Checklist: [x] schema projection implementation [x] streaming envelope framing [x] deterministic selection policy [x] docs + SDK examples [x] integration tests [x] feature flag gating [x] roll-out plan.
commits: feat(compat): add invocation envelope bridge and schema projection layer
perf(stream): minimize envelope allocation during fragment emission
test(openai): add deterministic-tool-selection unit tests and e2e streaming scenario
docs(compat): document bridge config and migration guidance
chore: add feature flag and rollout ci job
review_comments: Miguel Ortiz: Please double-check the tiebreaker deterministic seed. If schema ids can change during migration we should use stable route-scoped ids.
Author (Leah Kim): Good point. Updated schema_map to expose a stable_schema_id derived from route id + tool name and added a migration note so operators can pin the id if they reprocess prompts.
Samantha Li: e2e failed once on CI with a streaming fragment out of order. Is that covered by the envelope header?

Author (Leah Kim): The failure reproduced a race in the test harness only. The envelope header carries sequence and tool_id; I added stricter ordering checks in framer_test and fixed a subtle off-by-one in the fragment assembler.
Ravi Desai: Can we measure cost impact? The bench looks okay but we need to track real traffic before rolling out wide.
Author (Leah Kim): Added microbench results to docs and a rollout plan that ramps 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring dashboards and alerting on p99 token latency regression.
ci_flaky_notes: Integration e2e test was flaky once. Rerun green. Added deterministic test harness to prevent regression.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in OpenAI compatibility bridge that standardizes function/tool invocation envelopes and deterministic tool-selection semantics. Operators can enable per-route via openai_compat.bridge=true. Backward-compatible when disabled. Includes SDK examples and migration notes.
migration_steps: 1) Enable OPENAI_COMPAT_BRIDGE on a single canary route. 2) Monitor p99 token latency and tool-invocation mismatch metric. 3) Ramp according to rollout plan in docs. 4) If customer relies on historical ambiguous selection, pin stable_schema_id and consider reprocessing prompts.
notes_for_release_engineering: Feature flag gating requires a config toggle export and a migration dashboard. Please include the new OPENAI_COMPAT_BRIDGE in deploy templates and provision the dashboard linked in docs/openai-compatibility-guide.md.
testing_summary: Unit tests for projection and tiebreaker added. Integration e2e verifies streaming fragments with envelope headers. Microbench harness measures p50/p95/p99 token latency impact. SDK examples tested against local bridge.
security_considerations: No new privileged surface. Schema projection may reveal tool parameter names in the streaming envelope; sensitive parameter values are never included and follow existing data protection rules. Reviewed by security scans.
customers_impacted: none by default. Opt-in bridge. Early internal customers testing as part of ENG-4123.
notes: This PR prefers conservative defaults and explicit operator enablement to avoid surprising behavior. Follow rollout plan before enabling broadly.
